questions.q: What question does the summary suggest asking to judge whether an opportunity is good enough?
a: Would I give up everything I am working on now for it?
Could I start it without leaving my current job?
Will it attract investors within the first year?
Does anyone else in my field think it will work?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says an opportunity is worth pursuing if you believe it justifies abandoning your current work.

questions.q: Why did Daymond John work as a waiter while starting FUBU?
a: The income kept him afloat until he got funding
He wanted to learn how restaurants manage staff
He was saving money to attend business school
The restaurant let him sell clothes to customers
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the waiter job as a parachute that supported him until FUBU raised millions.

questions.q: How did 5-hour Energy stand out in a market dominated by Big Soda?
a: It sold small two-ounce bottles instead of standard sizes
It charged far less than every competing drink
It advertised only in gyms and health stores
It offered a wider range of flavors than rivals
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Bhargava chose two-ounce bottles rather than the standard sizes everyone else used.

questions.q: What does the Zuckerberg quote in the summary say influences people most?
a: A recommendation from a trusted friend
A memorable television advertisement
A low price compared with competitors
A famous person endorsing the product
questions.why: Lesson 2 cites Zuckerberg saying nothing influences people more than a trusted friend's recommendation.

questions.q: What did Johnson & Johnson do when Tylenol bottles were tampered with?
a: It recalled every bottle in the United States
It lowered the price to regain customer trust
It blamed the tampering on a former employee
It stopped selling Tylenol permanently
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the company recalled all US bottles despite discouragement from the FBI and FDA.
